draft.title: Sole traders and partnerships
card: An unincorporated business is not a legal entity separate from its owners. In the eyes of the law, the owners and the business are the same.
a business with one owner, who keeps all the profit and makes all the decisions.
a business with two or more owners, who share the profit and the work.
These businesses are easy and cheap to start. But the owners have unlimited liability: if the business cannot pay its debts, they can lose their own assets, such as their car or home.
draft.remember: Sole traders and partnerships are cheap to start, but the owners' own assets are at risk.

a.q: Which statement correctly describes a sole trader?
opts: One owner who can lose personal assets to pay business debts
One owner whose personal assets are safe from business debts
Two or more owners who share the profit and the risk
A business that is a separate legal entity from its owner
a.why: A sole trader has one owner, and the law treats the owner and the business as one. So the owner has unlimited liability. The second option is tempting, but it describes limited liability, which unincorporated businesses do not have.
a.clue: Think about who is responsible when the business cannot pay.

b.q: Priya and Tom run a plumbing business in Bathurst as partners. A client sues, and the business cannot pay the court order. What could happen?
opts: Their own assets, such as a car, could be used to pay it
Only the money the business holds could be taken
Only the assets of the partner who did the job are at risk
Neither partner is liable, as the business is a separate entity
b.why: A partnership is unincorporated, so the owners have unlimited liability. Their personal assets can be used to pay the business's debts. The last option is tempting, but a separate legal entity applies to incorporated businesses, not partnerships.
b.clue: Is a partnership separate from its owners in the eyes of the law?

proposal.title: Sole traders and partnerships
card: An unincorporated business is not a legal entity separate from its owners. In the eyes of the law, the owners and the business are the same.
a business with one owner, who keeps all the profit and makes all the decisions.
a business with two or more owners, who share the profit and the work. Each partner can be made to pay all of the business's debts, not just their share.
These businesses are easy and cheap to start. But the owners have unlimited liability: if the business cannot pay its debts, they can lose their own assets, such as their car or home.
proposal.remember: Sole traders and partnerships are cheap to start, but the owners' own assets are at risk.

a.q: Which statement correctly describes a sole trader?
opts: One owner who can lose personal assets to pay business debts
One owner whose personal assets are safe from business debts
Two or more owners who share the profit and the risk
A business that is a separate legal entity from its owner
a.why: A sole trader has one owner, and the law treats the owner and the business as one. So the owner has unlimited liability. 'One owner whose personal assets are safe from business debts' is tempting, but it describes limited liability, which unincorporated businesses do not have.
a.clue: Think about who is responsible when the business cannot pay.

b.q: Priya and Tom run a plumbing business in Bathurst as partners. A client sues, and the business cannot pay the court order. What could happen?
opts: Their own assets, such as a car, could be used to pay it
Only the money the business holds could be taken
Only the assets of the partner who did the job are at risk
Nothing, as the partnership is a separate legal entity
b.why: A partnership is unincorporated, so the owners have unlimited liability, and each partner can be made to pay the business's debts. 'Nothing, as the partnership is a separate legal entity' is tempting, but being a separate legal entity applies to incorporated businesses, not partnerships.
b.clue: Is a partnership separate from its owners in the eyes of the law?
